ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the Arabic sentence أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My name is Ahmad.
   B. I am a pupil (boy).
   C. I am from Kenya.
   D. I am a pupil (girl).

2. Which Arabic word means "thank you"? (1 mark)
   A. مَسَاءُ الْخَيْرِ
   B. مَرْحَبًا
   C. اسْمِي
   D. شُكْرًا

3. Which Arabic sentence means "I am from Kenya." (1 mark)
   A. اسْمِي أَحْمَدُ
   B. أَنَا مِنْ كينيا
   C. أَنَا تِلْمِيذَةٌ
   D. أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ

4. Which is a good way of caring for household items? (1 mark)
   A. Throw books on the floor
   B. Leave a lamp near water
   C. Wash cups and plates after use
   D. Leave a knife within reach of small children

5. What does the Arabic word ayna ask? (1 mark)
   A. Where
   B. Who
   C. Why
   D. What

6. What does the Arabic sentence هَذَا بَيْتِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. The cat is under the bed.
   B. The book is on the table.
   C. The lamp is above the table.
   D. This is my house.

7. Which Arabic sentence means "Today is Thursday." (1 mark)
   A. أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ
   B. فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ سَبْعَةُ أَيَّامٍ
   C. أَلْعَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ
   D. الْيَوْمُ يَوْمُ الْخَمِيسِ

8. What does hal do at the start of an Arabic question? (1 mark)
   A. It means 'and'
   B. It means 'the'
   C. It means 'my'
   D. It makes a yes or no question

9. What does the Arabic sentence أُحِبُّ الْعَصِيرَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I like bananas.
   B. I like juice.
   C. I drink water.
   D. I eat bread.

10. What does the Arabic sentence أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I hear with my ear.
   B. I smell with my nose.
   C. I speak with my mouth.
   D. I see with my eye.

11. What does the Arabic sentence الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is cloudy.
   B. The weather is cold.
   C. The weather is hot.
   D. The weather is rainy.

12. What does the Arabic sentence الْجَوُّ مُمْطِرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The weather is cloudy.
   B. The weather is hot.
   C. The weather is cold.
   D. The weather is rainy.

13. What does the Arabic sentence شُكْرًا لِاسْتِمَاعِكُمْ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I am in Grade 4.
   B. Water is useful (good for you).
   C. In my house there is a kitchen.
   D. Thank you for listening.

14. How is the syllable بِي read? (1 mark)
   A. buu
   B. bi
   C. bii
   D. bay

15. Which sound does the Arabic letter ز make? (1 mark)
   A. t as in tap
   B. z as in zebra
   C. j as in jug
   D. k as in kite

16. What is the name of the Arabic letter ق? (1 mark)
   A. Haa
   B. qaaf
   C. DHaa
   D. Daad

17. How is the Arabic word عَمَّةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ibn
   B. ab
   C. ʿamma
   D. ukht

18. Which sentence means 'On the table there is a cake'? (1 mark)
   A. ʿalaa t-taawilati kaʿka
   B. hadiyya li-Aminata
   C. fawqa t-taawilati baaluun
   D. haadhihi hafla

19. What does the Arabic sentence الْعَصِيرُ بَارِدٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The fish is delicious.
   B. Water is useful (good for you).
   C. The juice is cold.
   D. I like food.

20. What does qawiyy mean? (1 mark)
   A. small
   B. strong
   C. hot
   D. new

21. What does the Arabic sentence لِي عَيْنَانِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My body is strong.
   B. This is my body.
   C. I have two hands.
   D. I have two eyes.

22. How is the Arabic word غَائِمٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. mushmis
   B. ghaa'im
   C. shams
   D. haarr

23. What does maa ajmala l-bii'a mean? (1 mark)
   A. The rain is heavy.
   B. How beautiful the environment is!
   C. Where is the environment?
   D. I plant a tree.

24. Which Arabic sentence means "And the rain is from the sky." (1 mark)
   A. الشَّمْسُ فِي السَّمَاءِ
   B. وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ
   C. رَأْسِي كَبِيرٌ
   D. مَا أَجْمَلَ الْبِيئَةَ

25. Which Arabic sentence means "Do not play with the knife." (1 mark)
   A. عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كُوبٌ
   B. لَا تَلْعَبْ بِالسِّكِّينِ
   C. الْكُرْسِيُّ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ
   D. الْمِفْتَاحُ فِي الْخِزَانَةِ

26. How is the Arabic word تَحْتَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ʿinda
   B. fii
   C. amaama
   D. taHta

27. How is the Arabic word مِلْعَقَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. baab
   B. qalam
   C. hadiiqa
   D. milʿaqa

28. How many forms can an Arabic letter have at most? (1 mark)
   A. Four: alone, start, middle and end
   B. Six
   C. Two
   D. One

29. What is the name of the Arabic letter ف? (1 mark)
   A. taa
   B. faa
   C. shiin
   D. Saad

30. Which letter has one dot above it? (1 mark)
   A. ب (baa)
   B. ي (yaa)
   C. ت (taa)
   D. ن (nuun)

31. What is the ending of the letter ة in جَدَّةٌ called? (1 mark)
   A. hamza
   B. taa marbuta
   C. sukuun
   D. shadda

32. What does at-taawilatu Sagiira mean? (1 mark)
   A. The table is small.
   B. The chair is new.
   C. The door is clean.
   D. The table is big.

33. What does the Arabic sentence النَّافِذَةُ نَظِيفَةٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The chair is new.
   B. The door is big.
   C. The window is clean.
   D. The table is small.

34. Which two letters begin the names of the days of the week in Arabic script (the word 'the')? (1 mark)
   A. baa and taa
   B. miim and nuun
   C. siin and shiin
   D. alif and laam

35. Which Arabic word means "Monday"? (1 mark)
   A. الْيَوْمَ
   B. الِاثْنَيْنِ
   C. غَدًا
   D. الثُّلَاثَاءُ

36. Which word fills the gap in: ashrabu ____ (I drink the juice)? (1 mark)
   A. baaluun
   B. al-kaʿka
   C. al-ʿasiira
   D. al-hafla

37. Which Arabic sentence means "We dance." (1 mark)
   A. عِنْدِي هَدِيَّةٌ
   B. نَحْنُ نَرْقُصُ
   C. أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ الطَّعَامَ
   D. أَنَا أُحِبُّ الْحَفْلَةَ

38. Which Arabic sentence means "I eat rice." (1 mark)
   A. الْمَوْزُ لَذِيذٌ
   B. رَأْسِي كَبِيرٌ
   C. أَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ
   D. آكُلُ الْأَرُزَّ

39. Which Arabic word means "apples"? (1 mark)
   A. جَدَّةٌ
   B. رِجْلٌ
   C. تُفَّاحٌ
   D. صَدِيقٌ

40. What does the Arabic word جَوٌّ (jaww) mean? (1 mark)
   A. wind
   B. weather
   C. cloudy
   D. rainy

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Translate into English: ʿindii akh wa ukht (2 marks)

42. Translate into English: azraʿu shajara (2 marks)

43. Write four lines of a short conversation in which two friends greet each other and ask names. Use English letters for the Arabic. (4 marks) (4 marks)

44. List four characteristics of good handwriting. (4 marks) (4 marks)

45. Write a three-sentence paragraph about your room in Arabic sounds and give the meaning. (5 marks) (5 marks)

46. Translate into English: nuhaafidhu ʿalaa l-bii'a (2 marks)

47. Translate into English: anaa uhibbu l-hafla (2 marks)

48. Describe how you can make flashcards for the days of the week. (3 marks) (3 marks)

49. Translate into English: ʿindii hadiyya (2 marks)

50. Give three examples of non-verbal cues you could use when reciting a poem about weather. (3 marks) (3 marks)

51. Give the steps for reading a new Arabic word. (3 marks) (3 marks)

52. Translate into English: azuuru jaddatii yawma l-jumuʿa (2 marks)

53. Explain why untidy handwriting can be a problem in Arabic. (2 marks) (2 marks)

54. Describe how a class can make a letter bank. (3 marks) (3 marks)

55. Translate into English: al-asdiqaa'u fii l-hafla (2 marks)

56. Translate into English: anaa bi-khayr, al-hamdu lillaah (2 marks)

57. Translate into English: fii l-usbuuʿi sabʿatu ayyaam (2 marks)

58. Write two describing words in Arabic sounds with their meanings, one for a masculine and one for a feminine item. (3 marks) (3 marks)

59. Translate into English: haadhihi ummii (2 marks)

60. Translate into English: al-mawzu ladhiidh (2 marks)

61. Translate into English: anaa tilmiidh (2 marks)

62. Translate into English: unadhdhifu asnaanii (2 marks)

63. Copy and translate the sentence أُحِبُّ الْخُبْزَ. (2 marks) (2 marks)

64. Read the sentence اسْمِي أَحْمَدُ and write its meaning. (2 marks) (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — I am a pupil (boy).
   أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ (anaa tilmiidh) means: I am a pupil (boy).

2. D — شُكْرًا
   شُكْرًا (shukran) means thank you.

3. B — أَنَا مِنْ كينيا
   أَنَا مِنْ كينيا (anaa min Kiiniya) means: I am from Kenya.

4. C — Wash cups and plates after use
   Cleaning items after use helps them to last and keeps the home safe.

5. A — Where
   ayna means 'where'.

6. D — This is my house.
   هَذَا بَيْتِي (haadhaa baytii) means: This is my house.

7. D — الْيَوْمُ يَوْمُ الْخَمِيسِ
   الْيَوْمُ يَوْمُ الْخَمِيسِ (al-yawmu yawmu l-khamiis) means: Today is Thursday.

8. D — It makes a yes or no question
   hal begins a question that can be answered with naʿam or laa.

9. B — I like juice.
   أُحِبُّ الْعَصِيرَ (uhibbu l-ʿasiira) means: I like juice.

10. C — I speak with my mouth.
   أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي (atakallamu bi-famii) means: I speak with my mouth.

11. C — The weather is hot.
   الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ (al-jawwu haarr) means: The weather is hot.

12. D — The weather is rainy.
   الْجَوُّ مُمْطِرٌ (al-jawwu mumtir) means: The weather is rainy.

13. D — Thank you for listening.
   شُكْرًا لِاسْتِمَاعِكُمْ (shukran li-istimaaʿikum) means: Thank you for listening.

14. C — bii
   The letter yaa after a kasra makes the vowel long, so بِي is bii.

15. B — z as in zebra
   The letter ز makes the sound z as in zebra.

16. B — qaaf
   The letter ق is called qaaf.

17. C — ʿamma
   عَمَّةٌ is read ʿamma and means father's sister.

18. A — ʿalaa t-taawilati kaʿka
   ʿalaa means on, taawila is table and kaʿka is cake.

19. C — The juice is cold.
   الْعَصِيرُ بَارِدٌ (al-ʿasiiru baarid) means: The juice is cold.

20. B — strong
   qawiyy means strong.

21. D — I have two eyes.
   لِي عَيْنَانِ (lii ʿaynaani) means: I have two eyes.

22. B — ghaa'im
   غَائِمٌ is read ghaa'im and means cloudy.

23. B — How beautiful the environment is!
   maa ajmala is a cry of wonder meaning 'how beautiful'.

24. B — وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ
   وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ (wal-maTaru mina s-samaa'i) means: And the rain is from the sky.

25. B — لَا تَلْعَبْ بِالسِّكِّينِ
   لَا تَلْعَبْ بِالسِّكِّينِ (laa talʿab bi-s-sikkiin) means: Do not play with the knife.

26. D — taHta
   تَحْتَ is read taHta and means under.

27. D — milʿaqa
   مِلْعَقَةٌ is read milʿaqa and means spoon.

28. A — Four: alone, start, middle and end
   A joining letter can look different alone, at the start, in the middle and at the end of a word.

29. B — faa
   The letter ف is called faa.

30. D — ن (nuun)
   nuun has one dot above. Baa has one dot below, taa has two dots above and yaa has two dots below.

31. B — taa marbuta
   ة is taa marbuta and appears at the end of many feminine words.

32. A — The table is small.
   taawila is table and Sagiira means small.

33. C — The window is clean.
   النَّافِذَةُ نَظِيفَةٌ (an-naafidhatu nadhiifa) means: The window is clean.

34. D — alif and laam
   al- is written with alif and laam.

35. B — الِاثْنَيْنِ
   الِاثْنَيْنِ (al-ithnayn) means Monday.

36. C — al-ʿasiira
   We drink juice, not cake, a party or a balloon.

37. B — نَحْنُ نَرْقُصُ
   نَحْنُ نَرْقُصُ (nahnu narqusu) means: We dance.

38. D — آكُلُ الْأَرُزَّ
   آكُلُ الْأَرُزَّ (aakulu l-aruzza) means: I eat rice.

39. C — تُفَّاحٌ
   تُفَّاحٌ (tuffaah) means apples.

40. B — weather
   جَوٌّ (jaww) means weather.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: I have a brother and a sister.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: I plant a tree.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: A: as-salaamu ʿalaykum. B: wa ʿalaykumu s-salaam. A: maa ismuka? B: ismii Ahmad.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct line: greeting, reply, question, answer.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Correct letter shapes; letters the same size; letters on the baseline; correct dots and marks; even spacing; clean page.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid characteristic, up to 4.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example: haadhihi ghurfatii. fii l-ghurfati sariir. uhibbu ghurfatii. This is my room. In the room there is a bed. I like my room.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence, 1 mark for a beginning-middle-end order and 1 mark for the meaning.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: We look after the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like the party.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Cut cards; write the Arabic day on the front; write the English name and sound on the back; decorate and display in order.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: I have a gift.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lifting arms for the sun; wiggling fingers downwards for rain; smiling at the last line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cue that matches a word.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at each letter and its mark; read each syllable; blend the syllables and check that the word makes sense.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: I visit my grandmother on Friday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Letters that differ only by dots may look the same, so the reader may read the wrong word.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dots and 1 mark for the wrong reading.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give each group some letters; write each letter and its name on a card with a picture or word that begins with it; arrange the cards in order in the class portfolio.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for writing cards, 1 mark for adding names or words and 1 mark for arranging them.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: The friends are at the party.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: I am well, thanks be to God.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: There are seven days in a week.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: kabiir (big) for a masculine word and kabiira (big) for a feminine word.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each form and 1 mark for the meaning.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my mother.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: The banana is delicious.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: I am a pupil (boy).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

62. (2 marks)
   Answer: I clean my teeth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

63. (2 marks)
   Answer: uhibbu l-khubza. I like bread.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a correct copy or sounds and 1 mark for the translation.

64. (2 marks)
   Answer: ismii Ahmad. My name is Ahmad.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reading and 1 mark for meaning.
